prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: the two frame(s) of the 2-WAY MISSILE rocket — a compact steel rocket that alternates climbing up-to-the-right and diving down-to-the-right — one clear missile subject. The two cells are the SAME rocket in its two flight attitudes.

Design identity to keep exactly — the 2-WAY MISSILE: a compact chunky rocket about 150 px across its square footprint, centred in its 256×256 cell with a wide even band of flat key on every side. A light steel-grey body (#a0a8b8) with a 1-px dark navy-blue outline (#2a3a4a), a bright white nose cap (#ffffff) at its front tip, two short fins at the tail, and a small orange-red exhaust flare (#e84818) burning right at the tail — the exhaust stays tight against the rocket, inside the same footprint. Frame 0 slants up to the right at 45 degrees (nose upper-right); frame 1 is that SAME rocket slanted down to the right at 45 degrees (nose lower-right, the picture flipped top-to-bottom).

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- EXACTLY 2 cells laid out as 1 ROW OF 2 (2-column by 1-row) — every cell holding exactly ONE subject at the same scale and position; a missing, empty or merged cell ruins the entire sheet.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = FRAME 0 CLIMBING — the rocket slanted up to the right, white nose at the upper-right corner of its slant, orange exhaust at the lower-left tail. The subject lies within aspect 0.70:1 to 1.30:1.
  cell 2 = FRAME 1 DIVING — the SAME rocket drawn again, its exact top-to-bottom mirror: slanted down to the right, white nose at the lower-right, orange exhaust at the upper-left tail. The subject lies within aspect 0.70:1 to 1.30:1.
- MIRROR LAW: cell 2 is cell 1 turned upside-down — same rocket, same length, same thickness, same colours, same dead-centre position; only the slant direction flips (climb becomes dive). Both rockets share one square footprint of about 150 px inside their cells.
- SAME SUBJECT LAW: every cell shows the SAME subject, the same size, the same materials and colours, at the same position in its cell — only the named attitude changes between cells.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 512×256 px. Produce EXACTLY 2 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 12 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- CENTRING AND SIZE: every subject sits at the exact centre of its cell at the same scale and position as the other cell — only the named state changes.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: the finest retro pixel art for its native resolution — as much detail and inner structure as possible AT that low resolution, crisp hard-edged square pixels, chunky bold forms, a rich four-to-six step shading ramp lit from the top-left with careful inner detail and real material texture, clean saturated colours, a 1-px near-black outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, letters, labels, numbers, cell borders, guide lines, grid lines, watermark, signature, blurry, anti-aliasing, smooth gradient background, scenery, stars, cast shadow, drop shadow, multiple subjects per cell, empty cell, cropped subject, subject touching edge
